findings.title: Priority inversion: bm_high waited on bm_low via a mutex
findings.summary: bm_high (prio 30) was blocked 20.26 ms on a mutex (0x0000004579824070) released by bm_low (prio 10); for 20.25 ms of that, bm_low was ready but bm_med (prio 20) held its CPU. Seen 40x.
findings.qnx_note: QNX mutexes inherit priority by default; an inversion through a mutex means inheritance was disabled (PTHREAD_PRIO_NONE) or a priority ceiling is too low.

findings.title: Mutex contention hotspot at 0x0000004579824070
findings.summary: 1 threads waited 40 times (10/s) for mutex 0x0000004579824070; someone was waiting 20% of the time; p99 wait 20.26 ms.
findings.qnx_note: Every MUTEX-state interval is real contention: uncontended QNX mutexes never enter the kernel. Shrink the critical section (copy outside the lock), split the lock per resource, or hand buffers between threads with message passing.

findings.title: Unusual behaviour in bm_high
findings.summary: bm_high (prio 30) behaved unlike healthy QNX programs in 80 of its 80 time windows; the most unusual stretch lasted 80 ms. It stands out in: time blocked on a mutex (higher than healthy), time blocked while a lower-priority thread held its CPU (higher than healthy), longest single block (higher than healthy). The closest pattern TraceLens has seen is many threads serialised on one mutex, but only loosely (distance 10.55 against 1.716 typical for it): treat this as behaviour of its own.
findings.qnx_note: Learned from healthy QNX 8.0 traces: this thread behaved unlike any healthy run in the features listed. It is not a proven bug and gets no automatic fix: look at the timeline around it. Any resemblance to a known pattern is measured against labelled example windows, never a rule that fired.

findings.title: Unusual behaviour in bm_low
findings.summary: bm_low (prio 10) behaved unlike healthy QNX programs in 60 of its 80 time windows; the most unusual stretch lasted 20 ms. It stands out in: longest wait for a CPU (higher than healthy), time waiting for a CPU (higher than healthy), time asleep (lower than healthy). The closest pattern TraceLens has seen is an interrupt handler working with its line still masked (distance 0.53, inside the 0.705 typical for that pattern).
findings.qnx_note: Learned from healthy QNX 8.0 traces: this thread behaved unlike any healthy run in the features listed. It is not a proven bug and gets no automatic fix: look at the timeline around it. Any resemblance to a known pattern is measured against labelled example windows, never a rule that fired.
